question.leadin: This city-state was led by kings from two lines, the Agiads and Eurypontids, simultaneously.
question.text: Name this Ancient Greek city-state, also led by five ephors [ay-fors]and the Gerousia [yeh-roo-shee-ah] elder council, a militaristic rival to Athens during the Peloponnesian War.
question.clue: Every autumn, this city redeclared war on the enslaved helots.

swap.text: This Greek known as the "Father of History" wrote the main surviving account of the Greco-Persian Wars.
swap.clue: This author likely confused marmots for giant gold-digging ants in India.

question.leadin: Give the following about famously terse replies in history.
question.text: After subduing Theban and Athenian forces, this Macedonian king and father of Alexander the Great sent an envoy to Sparta, saying "Surrender now, because if we invade, we will kill you and tear down your city." Sparta's one-word reply, "If.", convinced this man to leave Sparta alone.
question.answerHtml: Philip II of Macedon (prompt on partial answer)
question.clue: This leader was killed by a man that Cleitarchus claims had been sexually abused by Attalus.

swap.leadin: The introduction of the sarissa pike by this country's Philip II revolutionized its military.
swap.text: Name this ancient country that gained control of Greece after winning at Chaeronea. A modern country of this name has capital at Skopje.
swap.answerHtml: Macedonia [accept Macedon, prompt “Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia” or “Fyrom” ]
swap.clue: This kingdom, which was annexed by Rome after the Battle of Pydna, formed a federation of Greek cities called the League of Corinth after it defeated Thebes at the Battle of Chaeronea.

question.leadin: This figure had a widely disapproved affair with Aspasia of Miletus.
question.text: Identify this 5th century BC politician who oversaw the construction of the Parthenon and championed democracy, leading Thucydides to call him the "first citizen of Athens."
question.clue: This man developed a grand strategy that involved not facing the army of Sparta, but instead foiling their plan for victory.

swap.text: This Athenian admiral and statesmen led the Greek fleet after earlier convincing the Athenian assembly to fund its construction. He was later ostracized by Cimon.
swap.clue: This man correctly interpreted the prophecy that "wooden walls will defend you and your children."

question.leadin: Name these things about the Persian Wars.
question.text: Leonidas and three hundred Spartans died defending a narrow mountain path in this battle.
question.clue: During this battle, a force including Demophilus' Thespians was attacked from behind after Ephialtes ("eh-fi-AL-tees") revealed a Phocian-guarded path to Xerxes.

swap.leadin: The partition of Babylon appointed one of these people named Perdiccas as a regent.
swap.text: Name these generals who replaced the earlier Hetairoi ("het-ay-roi") leaders of the companion cavalry. These people fought several namesake wars after a dying Macedonian King left his empire "to the strongest."
swap.clue: Conflict between these people began when their former leader granted his kingdom "to the strongest."

question.text: The Bronze Age Collapse ended the use of this written script, the only one in the Mycenaean language that has been deciphered.
question.clue: This system consists of ninety syllabic signs, all of which correspond to open syllables.

swap.text: This German's boyhood dream was fulfilled on the hills of Hissarlik, Turkey, when he found Troy. He also excavated Mycenae, Ithaca, Orchomenus, and Tiryns.
swap.clue: One of this man's most famous discoveries was a golden burial mask belonging to a Mycenaean king, which this archaeologist presumed was Agamemnon.

question.text: The Helot population comprised almost entirely of residents from the south of this peninsula, where the city of Sparta is located. This peninsula's north contains the city of Delphi.
question.answerHtml: the Peloponnese [or Peloponnesian peninsula or Peloponnesia or Peloponnesus or Morea; prompt on Greek peninsula]
question.clue: It's not in Algeria, but Jean-Baptiste Bory de Saint-Vincent directed a scientific commission that accompanied an 1828 military expedition to this region.

swap.leadin: This ruler led a victorious coalition at Heraclea, and he was killed by a falling roof tile at Argos.
swap.text: Name this king of Epirus, who names a type of victory that is as costly as a defeat.
swap.clue: Lysimachus ended this man's short first reign as King of Macedon, but this man later regained that title shortly before he died in Argos.

question.text: This civilization who wrote in Linear A is said to possibly be part of the Sea Peoples. This Aegean culture built a palace at Knossos and is named after a mythical king who ordered a king of Athens to send 14 young people to his domain at tribute.
question.clue: One of this civilization's palaces is where the mysterious Phaistos disc was found.

swap.leadin: After he was tried for failing to capture this city, one monarch explained that because he had really captured a nearby forest of the same name, he had fulfilled an oracle's prophecy.
swap.text: Name this city that was the origin and namesake of the Macedonian royal family. This city engaged in the Battle of the Champions with its longtime rival, Sparta.
swap.clue: Weights and measures found at the Heraion of this city are said to date to the reign of King Pheidon, who ruled this city as a tyrant.

question.text: Bedrich ("bed-REEK") Hrozny, the decipherer of the Hittite language, proposed that the Ahhiyawa ("a-HI-ya-WA") ruled from this island. Chares of Lindos built a bronze sculpture to commemorate Demetrius I's failed siege of this island.
question.clue: Previously this polity had been a powerful federal state dominating the commercial traffic of the Eastern Mediterranean through its five ports.

swap.text: This man put his son Agathocles to death on charges of treason. This ally of Cassander and Seleucus at Ipsus was King of Asia Minor, Macedon, and Thrace when he was slain in the 281 BCE battle of Corupedium.
swap.clue: Despite his successful defence of Lydia and Caria against Demetrius I Poliorcetes, this man's son Agathocles was still put to death, resulting in an enemy invasion of this man's domains.

question.leadin: In contrast to his student, who wrote The Argonautica, this poet argued that Homer should not be emulated and that long poems exemplified the dictum "Big Book, Big Evil."
question.text: Name this Hellenistic poet who wrote the Pinakes, a catalog of the authors in a certain institution that is sometimes considered to be the first bibliography.

swap.leadin: Prior to this battle, the winning commander saw the daughters of Scedasus weeping at their tombs, but instead of sacrifcing a blonde virgin as he was asked, he sacrifced a flly with a red mane that burst into his camp.
swap.text: Name this ancient battle which ended with the defeat and death of king Cleombrotus I.
swap.clue: The victorious commander here put 50-men-deep columns on his left flank, allowing Pelopidas's men to crush the opposing Royal Bodyguard.

question.leadin: In this passage an invading army dismisses their weaker opponents' expression of hope in the gods with the dictum that "The strong do what they can; the weak suffer what they must."
question.text: Name this important passage for the Realist School of International Relations, a section of the History of the Peloponnesian War.
question.clue: A party in this passage notes that "the Cretan Sea is a wide one" to explain how a man such as Brasidas could evade a blockade.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about wars from Archaic Greek history that we don't really know anything about, FTPE.
swap.text: A series of wars in the eighth and seventh centuries led to Sparta's conquest of this region of the Peloponnese, whose inhabitants were the original Helots.
swap.clue: This Peloponnesian region that fought three wars, including two in the Archaic Period, with a neighboring polis. Demand for this region's fertile land, or kleroi, likely helped cause the first of those conflicts.
